scope: Independent design critique of twelve App Store listing stills only. Original-scale images and both rendered galleries inspected on 2026-09-29. Preview videos, upload processing, runtime accessibility, and canonical app-wide design are outside this verdict.

productContext.taskSubtype: App Store feature presentation for a numbered group-name picker
productContext.firstUser: Teacher, host, streamer, or group organizer
productContext.primaryJob: Recognize list entry, draw modes, traceable winner, no-repeat history, and safe reset
productContext.intendedEmotion: Confidence in an identifiable result, with playful celebration

categoryEvidence.audienceResonance: 01 pairs an identifiable numbered winner with celebration; 02–06 prove the host controls. The dominant display font and long celebratory card suit live-group energy more than quiet utility use.
categoryEvidence.categoryRecognition: 03 shows one large draw action beside a numbered pool; 04 shows the actual vertical wheel. Unlike radial-wheel references, the category is established by the complete sequence rather than every isolated blurred tile.
categoryEvidence.productSpecificity: Stable contestant IDs, active-pool checks, no-repeat history, a numbered result, and the guitar celebration identify NameSnap. Generic group names remain intentionally synthetic.
categoryEvidence.primaryTaskClarity: All twelve frames have a distinct action-led headline and visible evidence. Phone 03 and 04 make the active draw mode especially clear; iPad 05 requires closer inspection of its smaller history.
categoryEvidence.visualHierarchy: The headline leads to a complete feature artifact, then a footer. Phone 05 prioritizes result/history. iPad 05 keeps the draw setup and wheel above the history, so the history is less dominant.
categoryEvidence.compositionDiversity: Within one listing, 01 celebration, 02 editor, 03 circular action, 04 vertical picker, 05 history, and 06 confirmation vary the product object. The outer eyebrow/headline/frame/footer skeleton remains consistent, and iPad 03–06 have similar silhouettes.
categoryEvidence.contentRealism: The synthetic 16-name roster is plausible and consistently numbered. Phone 05 shows 12 Leo / 9 Priya / 7 Ava, 13 remaining; iPad 05 shows one prior winner, 9 Priya, and 15 remaining. These are demonstration states, not evidence of random outcomes.
categoryEvidence.domainArtifactFidelity: Every slide uses captured implemented UI; numbered names and current states are readable at original scale. Some lists extend under the native fixed toolbar because they are scroll views.
categoryEvidence.crossScreenContinuity: Maya #1, Jordan #2, Sofia #3, Liam #4 persist. Ava #7 in the hero also appears in phone history; phone remaining IDs visibly skip 7 and 9. iPad and phone are independent example runs, and the hero-first sequence is editorial rather than chronological.
categoryEvidence.platformFidelity: Phone status area and home indicator are intact in full-screen frames; iPad toolbar ends are now complete. Cropped detail frames deliberately omit the status area. The reset toolbar remains undimmed behind the modal in the actual UI, a pre-existing presentation limitation.
categoryEvidence.spatialEconomy: Phone frames make strong use of the canvas. iPad 03–06 preserve source width and aspect but leave a broad background gap above the footer; iPad 01 also devotes substantial room to confetti. These reduce efficiency without hiding the feature.
categoryEvidence.typography: Headline, result, count badges, main names, and actions are readable at original resolution. Heavy all-caps display type is reserved mainly for branding/actions. Tablet metadata and footer text become small at gallery scale. The final iPad 04 caption is now the directly supported Keep every contestant tied to a clear number.
categoryEvidence.accessibility: Dark labels, outlined actions, explicit Cancel/Reset wording, numbered names, and checkmarks provide visible non-color cues. Fading wheel neighbors and small celebration metadata are weaker, but the centered current option is readable. Still-image review cannot verify VoiceOver, dynamic type, focus, or reduced motion.
categoryEvidence.interactionCredibility: Add, mode choice, Spin, checked pool rows, no-repeat toggle, history, and reset dialog look implementable and match captured app objects. Screenshots do not prove tap execution or draw randomness.
categoryEvidence.stateCompleteness: For a six-slide listing, pre-add disabled draw, ready modes, winner success, no-repeat history, and reset confirmation cover the advertised story. Empty/exhausted/error/offline states are not shown and are not being certified.
categoryEvidence.distinctiveness: The numbered celebration medal, illustrated reveal, offset violet outlines, and warm action buttons form an identifiable NameSnap signature. Some pill and rounded-panel treatment is repeated heavily.
categoryEvidence.appStorePlausibility: The stills are finished, coherent promotional assets using real app screens and one feature per slide; no placeholder charts or invented radial wheel appears. Tablet whitespace and smaller secondary copy are visible polish limitations.
categoryEvidence.implementationReadiness: The AppKit generator records fonts, colors, sources, sizes, crop parameters, and export handling; raw screenshots and the capture-only patch are retained. Recreating the live capture still depends on the simulator fixture setup.
categoryEvidence.componentSemantics: Winner #7 and Ava agree; phone result #12 and the first history item agree; history count and skipped active IDs agree; iPad #9 result/history and 15 active agree. A wheel's centered eligible option may differ from the separate last-result banner after a completed pick.
categoryEvidence.materialFit: Vibrant warm actions, violet depth, pale supporting panels, and playful artwork fit group entertainment while retaining legible utility controls. The repeated shadows are denser than the minimalist reference.

blurTest.evidence: Across the gallery, a winner medal, editable roster, central draw action, vertical picker, remaining-name list, and confirmation are identifiable without reading full copy. Celebration alone is less category-specific, but the suite is unambiguous.

silhouetteTest.evidence: The actual product objects change across 01–06. Repeated outer listing framing is intentional within one product, and is not being transplanted into unrelated product UI.

fiveSecondTest.evidence: Short action-led headings and direct artifacts distinguish paste, quick pick, wheel, no repeats, and reset; the winner name and number dominate phone 01.

realityTest.evidence: Real captured controls and plausible synthetic names are used. Counts show 16 ready/active, then 13 after three phone winners or 15 after one tablet winner. Fixture provenance is explicitly disclosed in the source document.

componentSemanticTest.evidence: Original-scale review covered editor rows/counts, draw-mode state, wheel selection, winner medal/name, recent-winner list, active-pool IDs/count, reset confirmation, and fixed toolbar. All visible labels/values agree. Captured source screens provide the unframed component evidence; no newly designed component is introduced.

journeyTest.evidence: The stable numbered roster connects setup, ready draw, reveal, history, and reset. Phone history includes hero winner Ava #7 and removes her from the visible eligible list. This is a feature showcase, not a single uninterrupted recording.

platformTest.evidence: Final screenshot framing retains complete active controls, source aspect, and phone/tablet-specific UI proportions. Status-bar collision and tablet toolbar side clipping from earlier passes are absent. Crop boundaries distinguish detail views from full-screen captures.

buyerValueTest.evidence: All twelve assets show finished NameSnap UI with concrete host benefits; none reads as a wireframe, generic dashboard, or planning slide.

implementationTest.evidence: Generator, source captures, capture viewport patch, and refresh document identify reproducible dimensions, font, color, screenshot provenance, and per-frame crop choices. No art has to be invented from a mockup.

categoryReferenceTest.evidence: Compared with current Apple-hosted Tiny Decisions, Spin The Wheel, and Decide Now examples. The suite uses the task grammar of an immediate draw/result and short benefit statement; it does not reproduce their radial wheels, aged device mockup, or busy paper framing. Marketing headings and framing remain outside the captured canonical UI.

referenceComparisons.evidence: One concise promise and a large real draw/result object informed category grammar; NameSnap keeps its own numbered pool and celebration art.
Recognizable selection/result mechanic is relevant. Busy paper background and dated device shell are treated as anti-patterns, not copied.
Action-led copy and direct product proof are relevant; NameSnap's vertical picker and outlined material remain distinct.

screenFindings.finding: Winner number 7 agrees with Ava Thompson and winner description. Close and both continuation actions are whole. iPad confetti has no opaque black rectangle; its hero figure is partly beyond the viewport as in the real celebration, not a clipped control.
16 READY and numbered input are legible. Disabled Spin is a valid pre-add state, although it occupies extra space below the input, especially on iPad.
Selected Quick Pick, large enabled Spin, 16 TOTAL, and named pool rows are clear. Final iPad toolbar now retains both rounded ends.

Selected Spin Wheel and centered Maya #1 are clear. Neighbor fading is native picker behavior. The repaired iPad caption Keep every contestant tied to a clear number is visible in the final render and is supported by the numbered wheel and active list.
Phone shows #12 Leo, history12/9/7, and13remaining; iPad shows #9Priya, history9, and15remaining. RECENT PICKS AT A GLANCE is now present in both rendered footers. Toolbar no longer clips sideways.

Reset dialog title, names-preserved explanation, Cancel, and Reset Pool are complete. The underlying main content is dimmed; the fixed toolbar stays bright in the existing UI. No new marketing-frame overlap is introduced.
A broad gap remains between framed detail and footer. This is a presentation economy limitation, not missing data or a clipped action.

repairs.action: Center the shorter detail frame within the available artifact region to distribute the leftover vertical space, retaining full source width and aspect. Reinspect after any change.

unverified: Preview video pixels, motion, transitions, and audio
App Store upload processing and ordering
Runtime focus, VoiceOver, dynamic type, reduced motion, and interaction behavior
Fairness/randomness claims beyond the separately tested implementation
Canonical UI outside the captured states
verdict: PASS for the twelve reviewed App Store listing stills, 93.25/100, with no critical rendered defect. This bounded design result does not approve preview videos, uploads, random-draw behavior, or app-wide accessibility. A fresh independent release pass remains required before customer-facing delivery.
